task: Run a KYC screen on Wirecard in Germany

nimble.claim: Wirecard AG legal name: Wirecard AG
Wirecard AG registry number: HRB 169227 (Amtsgericht München, register authority RA000304)
Wirecard AG LEI: 529900A8LX4KL0YUTH71 (entity status ACTIVE, LEI registration status LAPSED, last GLEIF update 2020-11-13)
Wirecard AG jurisdiction: Germany (DE), registered with the German commercial register at Amtsgericht München
Wirecard AG incorporation date: 1999-01-01 (founded 1 January 1999; became a public stock corporation in 2005 via reverse merger with InfoGenie AG)
Wirecard AG registered address: Einsteinring 35, 85609 Aschheim, Germany
Wirecard AG status: insolvent/defunct; filed for insolvency 25 June 2020 after €1.9bn was found missing; dismantled from 1 July 2020 and core business sold to Santander in November 2020
Markus Braun (Austrian) was CEO and CTO of Wirecard AG from January 2002 until resignation 19 June 2020 and dismissal on 30 June 2020; largest single shareholder (more than 7%)
Jan Marsalek (Austrian) was Chief Operating Officer and Management Board member of Wirecard 2010–2020, responsible for Asia business; dismissed 18 June 2020
Alexander von Knoop (von Koop) was Chief Financial Officer and Management Board member of Wirecard AG
James Freis was Interim CEO of Wirecard AG from 19 June 2020; former Director of FinCEN and former Group CCO of Deutsche Börse AG
Thomas Eichelmann was independent Supervisory Board member and Chairman of Wirecard AG since January 2020
Oliver Bellenhaus was a former Wirecard executive in Dubai, co-defendant in the Munich criminal trial and prosecution's key witness
Stephan von Erffa was Wirecard's former chief accountant and co-defendant in the Munich criminal trial
Michael Jaffé is the court-appointed insolvency administrator of Wirecard AG

PEP-adjacent flag: Markus Braun (former Wirecard CEO) was from 2017 listed as a member of the Staff Unit for Strategy, Analysis and Planning of Austrian Chancellor Sebastian Kurz; a Chancellery spokesperson later stated he had not worked in the unit
Sanctions: Jan Marsalek (former Wirecard COO) is subject to an INTERPOL red notice for fraud and listed among Germany BKA wanted fugitives (law-enforcement lists, not sanctions designations)
Adverse media: From April 2015 to 2019 FT Alphaville and FT investigations raised accounting-fraud allegations about Wirecard, which the company denied; later confirmed after the 2020 collapse

Adverse media: KPMG's special audit (2019–2020) of Wirecard could not verify the majority of 2016–2018 profits; EY failed to verify cash reserves in apparently fraudulent bank statements; BaFin referred misleading investor statements to prosecutors
Adverse media: Wirecard AG admitted €1.9bn in cash was missing (June 2020), shares fell almost 90%, EY refused to sign off accounts, and the company filed for insolvency on 25 June 2020

Adverse media: Markus Braun was detained 22 June 2020 on suspicion of accounting fraud and market manipulation, released on €5m bail, and re-arrested 22 July 2020; other former board members were also arrested

Adverse media: Jan Marsalek, former Wirecard COO, fled Germany, is subject to an Interpol red notice for fraud, is reportedly in Russia, and British authorities describe him as a Russian spy with links to GRU (Met Police, March 2025)
Adverse media: BaFin supervisory failure over Wirecard; the Bundestag announced an inquiry on 1 September 2020 and BaFin president Felix Hufeld and deputy Elisabeth Roegele left on 29 January 2021
Adverse media: Insolvency administrator Michael Jaffé dismantled Wirecard from 1 July 2020; the main business unit was sold to Santander for €100m in November 2020 and ~730 employees were laid off
Adverse media: In March 2022 Munich prosecutors charged Markus Braun with fraud, breach of trust and accounting manipulation (up to 15 years); Braun denies wrongdoing

Adverse media: Trial opened 8 December 2022 in Munich; Markus Braun, Oliver Bellenhaus and Stephan von Erffa face commercial gang fraud charges for falsifying Wirecard's financial statements since 2015, causing €3.1bn loss to banks; verdict expected 2026 or 2027

Adverse media: On 5 September 2024 Munich Regional Court I ordered former Wirecard board members including Markus Braun and the former CFO to pay EUR 140m plus interest for breaches of duty; Jan Marsalek was already under a partial default judgment for EUR 140m

Administration is ongoing.

Adverse media (high severity, 2024-08-06, embezzlement/fraud-related criminal proceedings): Reuters reported Munich prosecutors charged former Wirecard CFO Alexander von Knoop and former CPO Susanne Steidl with several counts of embezzlement; von Knoop was also charged with aiding and abetting embezzlement. Prosecutors alleged losses of several hundred million euros; the decision on trial was pending.

Adverse media (medium severity, 2025-11-13, insolvency litigation/shareholder claims): Germany's Federal Court of Justice held that Wirecard AG shareholders' capital-market damage claims are not ordinary insolvency claims and rank behind ordinary insolvency creditors; the court described allegations that Wirecard feigned a business model and misrepresented its assets, finances and profits.
